findings.reason: an implementer must pick one state, and whichever they pick half the section's own cases describe the other.
findings.text: s51's deliverable says an unreadable upstream "treats that one wait as unresolved", which in this plan's own vocabulary is the `awaiting-upstream` state that §2 releases when its last ref lands, but its done-when says the request is "stored held", and `held` is §10's state released only by a covering review or a coordinator; the two states have different release paths, so the third case ("repairing the upstream plan releases the held request on the next pass") describes a release `held` does not have

findings.reason: splitting it into two nodes lets each be gated and reviewed on one deliverable instead of a node whose gate proves neither cleanly.
findings.text: §50's deliverable carries two independent mechanisms: routing a refused request of an ended session to a live coordinator, and charging a hold to the session that placed it rather than the one that dispatched the run; the author signals this ("Separately, nova-00 reported …"), and the second mechanism has its own defect, its own module behaviour and its own done-when case, so a single verdict cannot close both

findings.reason: the granted scope cannot reach the surface the done-when tests, and the node would fail at dispatch exactly as the §41 write-path finding did.
findings.text: §52's endpoint requires "the server's plan write … refuse it", but the server patch path is `_handle_plan_write` in `reckon/serve.py:3827`, which does its own coverage check at `reckon/serve.py:3967` precisely because "The patch path renders its own HTML and never reaches the store's write paths"; `reckon/serve.py` is not among the section's write paths, so a node granted only `reckon/doccheck.py` and `reckon/_plan_html.py` cannot make the third case pass

findings.reason: a deliverable half of which no case measures can be silently unbuilt and still green.
findings.text: §52's deliverable names three write surfaces that must refuse a disagreeing file (audit-doc, the server's plan write, a promotion's plan commit), but the done-when has no case for the promotion path, whose plan commit goes through `_plan_html.write_state` at `reckon/crew/promotion.py:2250` and `:2457`; a node can pass every named case with promotion refusing nothing

findings.reason: the reported obligation is the section's actual product for the coordinator, so leaving its content untested lets a node pass while emitting a row that names no way to clear it.
findings.text: §49's deliverable requires the obligation to name "the refusal and what would clear it", and to cover refusals only a plan or coordinator change can clear (the section declared done, the plan terminal, the section no longer exists), but its done-when asserts only that the obligation appears, that the request is not retried, and that a store lock is still retried; no case asserts the obligation names the clearing action, and the plan-terminal and section-removed classes are never exercised
